name: Dolores Yeo
life: “I still remember the crooked diploma my father was too proud to show.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Dolores by a small Monday habit. Dolores watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I am paid for only one visit. I used the extra pair of hands to hang Dad's old framed diploma.
appearance: Dolores has close-cropped dark curls, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a black overshirt with pearl buttons. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Dolores rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Dolores keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Dolores wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
family: Leona Navarro is Dolores’s cousin. Dolores chooses an ordinary story to tell. Leona asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *A prize nobody entered*, Leona says, “I would like the piece read once to the people in it before anybody publishes a line.”
connections: Sam Rose. An old diploma goes on the wall during the overlap the accountant is examining.
